chunks: Sufyan al-Thawri passed by in the Sacred Mosque and saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wearing many expensive and fine clothes. He said: 'By God, I will go to him and rebuke him.' So he approached him and said: 'O son of the Messenger of God! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not wear such clothing, nor did Ali (peace be upon him), nor did anyone from your forefathers.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in a time of scarcity and financial straitness, and he used to take according to his straitness and his means. But the world after that has released its floodgates of abundance, and the most deserving of its people with it are its righteous ones.'
Then he recited: 'Say: Who has forbidden the adornments of God which He brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?'
'And we are the most rightful of those who take from it what God has granted. However, O Thawri, what you see on me of clothing — I wear it only for the people.'

Then he grasped Sufyan's hand and drew it toward himself, then raised the upper garment and showed a rough cloth beneath it against his skin. He said: 'This I wear for myself, and what you saw is for the people.' Then he pulled at Sufyan's upper garment — its outer layer was thick and coarse, and its inner part was soft. He said: 'You wore this outer garment for the people, and you wore this one for yourself, to please it.'

key_terms.أَبْرَار: The righteous, virtuous ones — those most deserving of worldly blessings
key_terms.أَرْخَتْ عَزَالِيَهَا: Released its floodgates — a metaphor for the world's abundance opening up in later generations
key_terms.زِينَةُ اللَّهِ: The adornments/beautifications that God created and permitted for His servants (Quran 7:32)
key_terms.قَتْر مُقْتِر: A time of severe scarcity and financial straitness; the Prophet's simplicity was context-specific

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Sadiq wear expensive clothes while claiming to follow the Prophet's example?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's (peace be upon him) encounter with Sufyan al-Thawri, a well-known Sunni ascetic scholar, in the Sacred Mosque during the Abbasid era. When challenged for wearing expensive clothes, the Imam provides a nuanced theological argument: the Prophet's austerity was situational and appropriate to his era of scarcity, whereas in times of abundance the righteous are the most entitled to God's bounties. Crucially, the Imam then reveals he privately wears rough inner garments for asceticism, and publicly wears fine clothes as a social duty — inverting Sufyan's hypocrisy of wearing coarse clothes in public for show while secretly wearing soft ones.

en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Once, Sufyan al-Thawriy passed by Masjid al-Haram (the sacred area) and he saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, dressed in fine expensive clothes. He decided to meet him (the Imam) and scold him. He went close and said, ‘O child of the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah did not dress up with this kind of dress, Ali did not dress with this kind of dress nor any of your ancestors did.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, lived at a time when it was a financially serious and stringent condition. He (the Messenger of Allah) lived according to such conditions but the world thereafter has become financially relaxed. The most deserving in financial opportunities are the virtuous people.’
He (the Imam) then read this verse, ‘Say, who has made unlawful the beautiful things that Allah has brought out for His servants and the fine kinds of means of sustenance.’ [7:31]
We are the most deserving of what Allah has granted. However, O Thawriy, what you see I have dressed up with I have done so for people.

He (the Imam) pulled his hand to himself and raised the outer layer of his dress. Underneath on his body was a layer of rough textured garment. He (the Imam) said, ‘I wear this for my own soul and what you see (the outer layer) is for people.’ He (the Imam) then raised the outer layer of the garment of Sufyan, which was of rough texture but the layer underneath on his body was of a fine quality. He (the Imam) said, ‘You have dressed up for people with the outer layer and for yourself to enjoy with the fine quality layer underneath.’”
